correctness.rationale: For rooted starlike posets with >=2 target arms, a nonroot point cannot map to target root because its source upset is a chain but the target-root upset branches. Every source arm maps to a terminal segment of one target arm as an order-preserving surjection, with binomial positive-composition count W_ij and full-arm count F_ij. A root bounded morphism exists precisely when each target arm is fully covered; inclusion-exclusion gives exact N and the defect PGF. Homogeneous factorial moments (k)_s(1-s rho/k)^r -> e^(-st) imply Poisson(e^-t) and the zero-defect probability. Independently enumerated raw finite bounded morphisms on five labelled arm-length pairs and matched exact formula.

evidence: Adam-Day et al. nerve-criterion results include qualitative existence conditions for starlike bounded-morphic images (cited Proposition 6.1); this does not specify weighted labelled multiplicities or a defect PGF. Classical coupon collector already proves the Poisson limit once categorical reduction gives per-arm probabilities; the probability theorem by itself is not new.
